name: Sermorelin / MOTS-c / NAD+
used_for: Marketed by clinics as a longevity stack addressing growth hormone signaling and cellular energy together.
summary: This blend pairs sermorelin, a growth hormone-releasing hormone fragment, and MOTS-c, an unapproved mitochondrial peptide, with NAD+, a coenzyme rather than a peptide (it has its own Library page, which is not a peptide page). No approved product contains the combination and no combination-specific human study was found. A clinic page says the rationale rests more on mechanism and limited research than on large human trials. Each component's own page holds the detailed information (Sermorelin, MOTS-c and NAD+); formulations vary by seller.

internet_claims.claim: A Miami anti-aging clinic's blog (Rewind Anti-Aging, which sells peptide therapy) describes sermorelin plus MOTS-c plus NAD+ as its most comprehensive anti-aging protocol, targeting aging at the cellular level.
The same clinic says most of its peptides are investigational or compounded and not FDA-approved for these uses.

dose.summary: No combination study was found, so there is no studied combined dose. One telehealth seller describes doses for the sermorelin and NAD+ pair, and the Miami clinic gives no doses for the three-part stack.

items.text: TrimRx, a telehealth seller, says for a sermorelin plus NAD+ pair: 200 to 500 mcg sermorelin under the skin before bed, 5 to 7 nights a week, with 250 to 500 mg NAD+ by vein once or twice a week or 300 to 600 mg sublingual NAD+ daily. The page does not cover MOTS-c.
items.label: internet

timing.summary: No study tested timing for the combination. Sellers describe the parts as given separately, with sermorelin at bedtime and NAD+ or MOTS-c in the morning.

items.text: TrimRx, a telehealth seller, says that in a sermorelin plus NAD+ pair the sermorelin is given before bed and the NAD+ in the morning, to avoid possible sleep disruption.
items.label: internet

items.text: PeptIQ, an education site with referral links to telehealth clinics, describes a MOTS-c plus oral NAD+ precursor (NMN or NR) routine with both taken in the morning, MOTS-c fasted or with a light meal. The page does not cover sermorelin and describes oral precursors, not NAD+ itself.
items.label: internet

frequency.summary: No study tested how often to give the three together. One clinic describes a different schedule for each part.

items.text: Rewind Anti-Aging, a Miami clinic that sells peptide therapy, says in its stack sermorelin is a nightly injection under the skin, MOTS-c is injected 3 to 5 times per week, and NAD+ is given by IV infusion as 2 to 4 infusions over 1 to 2 weeks and then monthly maintenance sessions.
items.label: internet

cycle_length.summary: No combined cycle length was studied. One referral-linked guide describes cycling for a MOTS-c plus NAD+ precursor pair.

items.text: PeptIQ, an education site with referral links to telehealth clinics, says for MOTS-c plus an oral NAD+ precursor: 8 to 12 weeks on and 4 weeks off for the MOTS-c, with the precursor continued through the break or taken 5 days on and 2 off. It describes this as based on mechanism, not human trials, and does not cover sermorelin.
items.label: internet

mechanism.summary: No study of the combination explains how it works. A clinic describes the rationale as covering growth hormone release, mitochondrial function and cellular repair.

items.text: Rewind Anti-Aging, a Miami clinic that sells peptide therapy, describes sermorelin plus MOTS-c plus NAD+ as its most comprehensive anti-aging protocol, aimed at aging at the cellular level through three routes: growth hormone optimization, mitochondrial function and cellular repair.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.summary: No approved product contains this combination. A clinic says most of its peptides are not FDA-approved for these uses.

items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: No combination data
side_effect_groups.summary: No combination safety or effectiveness study was found. Sellers argue from each part's mechanism, and one guide says no human trial compares the pair it covers.

items.text: PeptIQ, an education site with referral links to telehealth clinics, says no human trial directly compares MOTS-c with NAD+ and that the combination rests on mechanistic reasoning. The page does not cover sermorelin.
items.label: internet

items.text: Rewind Anti-Aging, a Miami clinic that sells peptide therapy, gives mechanisms for its three-part stack but cites limited clinical trial data specifically for the combination.
